rounds.fact: Pinterest launched by invite-only in 2010, and its signature masonry grid of pins was one of the first mainstream uses of that layout style on the web.
HotBot launched in 1996 with a distinctly loud, colorful interface, and was one of the first search engines to index the full text of pages rather than just titles and keywords.
Tripod was a major free website-builder alongside GeoCities and Angelfire, and was eventually bought by Lycos as part of its portal strategy in the late 90s.
Barnes & Noble launched bn.com in 1997 specifically to compete with Amazon, one of the first major traditional retailers to take online bookselling seriously.
Wired magazine's website carried over its distinctive, colorful print design into the browser, standing out at a time when most news sites still looked like plain digital newspapers.
